notes: Release Assistant playbook v1, from research/release-plan.md (checked 2026-11). Never edit a shipped version: copy it to the next version number instead. R is release day; offsets are days from R.

steps.title: Lock in a Friday release day
steps.what: Settle on the Friday this single comes out, about six weeks from now.
steps.why: New music goes out worldwide on Fridays at 00:01 local time, and Spotify's Release Radar refreshes on Fridays. Six weeks leaves room for the DistroKid upload, the Spotify pitch and the teasers.
steps.how: Check the date doesn't clash with anything big you have on, then keep it. Every other step in this plan is dated from it.

steps.title: Check your DistroKid plan allows a custom date
steps.what: Make sure your DistroKid plan lets you choose the release date.
steps.why: Only Musician Plus and Ultimate let you set a date weeks ahead. Without it you can't line up a Friday, and the R−21 upload and R−7 pitch can't be planned.
steps.how: In DistroKid, open your account plan. If it's Musician, upgrade to Musician Plus before you upload.

steps.title: Finish the master
steps.what: Get the final master of the track done and bounced.
steps.why: Everything else (the upload, the clips, the Canvas) is cut from the final file. Changing the audio after upload means re-delivering it.
steps.how: Bounce a 24-bit WAV of the final master and listen once on headphones, speakers and a phone before calling it done.

steps.title: Finish the artwork
steps.what: Make the cover art for the single.
steps.why: Stores reject artwork that breaks their rules, and a rejection costs days you may not have before R−21.
steps.how: Square, at least 3000 × 3000 px, JPG or PNG. No URLs, social handles, store logos or blurry images, and the text must match the artist and track names exactly.

steps.title: Request promo clips from the Visualizer
steps.what: Ask the Visualizer for about six 9:16 clips (15 s and 30 s) and a Canvas loop.
steps.why: Teasers start at R−14. Having the clips rendered early means the posting days never wait on a render.
steps.how: Pick 3 to 5 moments (the drop with about 2 s of lead-in, the build, the hook, the breakdown) and send the request. Clips come out clean, with no burned-in text, so you can add text in each app.

steps.title: Make the Spotify Canvas loop
steps.what: Get a short looping vertical video ready for Spotify Canvas.
steps.why: Canvas plays behind the track in the Spotify app. You upload it once the song shows under Upcoming, so it should be ready before then.
steps.how: 3 to 8 s, vertical 9:16, 720 to 1080 px tall, MP4. No text, no song or artist name, no fast cuts or strobing, and it should loop cleanly. The Visualizer's Canvas loop fits these specs.

steps.title: Check with DistroKid: Apple Music pitch and pre-adds
steps.what: Find out whether DistroKid pitches to Apple Music editors and sets up Apple pre-adds.
steps.why: Apple's pitch tool is for labels and distributors, so you probably can't pitch Apple yourself. It isn't confirmed what DistroKid does for you.
steps.how: Search DistroKid's help centre for Apple Music pitching and pre-adds, or ask their support. Note what they say for next time.

steps.title: Check with DistroKid: TikTok Pre-Release
steps.what: Find out whether a DistroKid delivery works with TikTok's Pre-Release tool.
steps.why: TikTok Pre-Release lets fans pre-save to Spotify and Apple Music from TikTok, but it isn't confirmed that DistroKid delivers early enough for it.
steps.how: Check DistroKid's help centre or support, and look in TikTok for Artists once the track is delivered.

steps.title: Write the short track description
steps.what: Write two or three sentences about the track: its sound, mood and story.
steps.why: Every other draft (the pitch, captions, emails) tells the same story when it starts from one description.
steps.how: Open the draft, edit it until it sounds like you, and keep it. Stick to facts you'd stand behind.

steps.title: Upload to DistroKid
steps.what: Upload the master and artwork to DistroKid with your custom release date.
steps.why: Uploading four weeks out leaves a week of slack for rejected artwork or a slow arrival in Spotify for Artists before the R−21 cutoff. On a first release, DistroKid needs four weeks to claim Spotify for Artists.
steps.how: In DistroKid, upload the single, set the release date to your Friday, and check every name and credit before you submit.

steps.title: Upload to SoundCloud as private
steps.what: Upload the track to SoundCloud and keep it private until release day.
steps.why: Going public on release day puts it in followers' feeds at the same time as every other store, and starts the 14-day amplification window.
steps.how: Upload as private with the artwork, title and tags filled in. Don't share the private link publicly.

steps.title: Pitch the song to Spotify editors
steps.what: Submit this one song to Spotify's editors as soon as it shows under Upcoming.
steps.why: Editors need time to listen, and a pitch also puts the song on your followers' Release Radar. You can only pitch one song at a time, and never once it's live.
steps.how: In Spotify for Artists, open Music, then Upcoming, and pitch the song. Fill in every field (genre, mood, instruments, story): more detail helps.

steps.title: Add the Canvas
steps.what: Upload the Canvas loop to the song in Spotify for Artists.
steps.why: Canvas is added once the song is under Upcoming, and it's there from the first play on release day.
steps.how: In Spotify for Artists, open the song under Upcoming and add the Canvas MP4.

steps.title: Share your HyperFollow pre-save link
steps.what: Put the DistroKid HyperFollow link in your bios and Stories.
steps.why: Spotify's Countdown Pages don't support singles. A HyperFollow pre-save also follows you on Spotify, which is what puts your next songs on fans' Release Radar.
steps.how: Copy the HyperFollow link from DistroKid and add it to your link-in-bio on every platform. Share it in a Story with a short clip.

steps.title: Refresh your Spotify profile
steps.what: Update your Spotify profile image and bio for this release.
steps.why: People who find the track will look at your profile next. Spotify's own release guide lists this as a pre-release step.
steps.how: In Spotify for Artists, open Profile and update the image and bio. Use the same bio elsewhere.

steps.title: Last day to upload to DistroKid
steps.what: The song must be uploaded to DistroKid by today.
steps.why: DistroKid says the release date must be at least three weeks out for Spotify playlist pitching. Upload later and the Spotify pitch and Release Radar are lost.
steps.how: If you haven't uploaded yet, do it today with your Friday release date.

steps.title: Switch to a TikTok Artist Account
steps.what: Make sure your TikTok is an Artist Account linked to your music.
steps.why: It links your sound to your artist profile and gives you TikTok's new-release tools, which highlight a new track from R−14 to R+30.
steps.how: DistroKid members can create one from the DistroKid dashboard in hours. Skip this if you already have one.

steps.title: Set up a Spotify Countdown Page
steps.what: Create a Countdown Page so fans can pre-save on Spotify itself.
steps.why: Pre-savers get a notification and the release in their library. Spotify only offers it for EPs and albums, to artists with 3,000 monthly listeners.
steps.how: In Spotify for Artists, open the release under Upcoming and create the Countdown Page within 72 hours of delivery.

steps.title: Send the track on LabelRadar
steps.what: Submit the track to a few labels and promoters on LabelRadar.
steps.why: Label A&Rs and promo channels look for tracks on LabelRadar, and a free submission reaches people beyond your followers.
steps.how: Pick 3 to 5 outlets that fit your subgenre, attach the private SoundCloud link, and add a short personal note.

steps.title: Start teasers with one audio snippet
steps.what: Post the first teaser on TikTok, Reels and Shorts, about three a week from now on.
steps.why: YouTube advises a teaser about two weeks out, and TikTok's New Release window opens at R−14. Using the same audio snippet in every clip groups the posts together. No platform gives a posts-per-week number, so the cadence is a default you can change.
steps.how: Use one of the promo clips and the same snippet every time. Upload the file to each app separately: watermarked reposts get less reach on Instagram.

steps.title: Send to 5 to 10 curators on SubmitHub or Groover
steps.what: Send the track to 5 to 10 curators for paid reviews.
steps.why: Curators who like it can add it to their playlists and share it. You pay for a review and a listen, never for a placement: buying placement or streams breaks Spotify's terms.
steps.how: Pick curators whose playlists fit your subgenre and recent picks. About $50 of the budget goes here.

steps.title: Email free curators and blogs
steps.what: Email a handful of independent playlist curators and blogs that accept submissions for free.
steps.why: Free outreach costs only time, and a few personal emails often beat a long list.
steps.how: Personalise each email with the recipient's name and why their outlet fits. Include the private SoundCloud link and release day.

steps.title: Point your Artist Pick at the release
steps.what: Set your Spotify Artist Pick to the upcoming release or your HyperFollow link.
steps.why: It sits at the top of your profile, so visitors see the new single first.
steps.how: In Spotify for Artists, open Profile, then Artist Pick, and choose the upcoming release if offered.

steps.title: Last day to pitch to Spotify
steps.what: The Spotify editorial pitch must be in by today.
steps.why: Spotify needs a pitch at least 7 days before release. It's also the cutoff for picking the song for your followers' Release Radar.
steps.how: If you haven't pitched yet, do it now in Spotify for Artists under Upcoming.

steps.title: Post daily teasers
steps.what: Post a short teaser every day from now until a week after release.
steps.why: The last week before release is when people decide to pre-save. Daily posting is a default, not a platform rule; change it if it burns you out.
steps.how: Rotate the promo clips and add self-filmed ideas on days with no clip (studio, drop reaction, talking to camera). Keep the same audio snippet.

steps.title: Schedule a YouTube Premiere
steps.what: Schedule the visualizer video as a YouTube Premiere on release day.
steps.why: YouTube recommends premiering the video the same day the song comes out.
steps.how: Upload the video in YouTube Studio, choose Premiere, and set it for release day.

steps.title: Schedule the SoundCloud release
steps.what: Schedule the private SoundCloud track to go public on release day.
steps.why: Scheduled release is an Artist Pro feature, and it means you don't have to be awake at midnight.
steps.how: On the track's edit page, set the release date and time to release day at 00:01.

steps.title: Make the SoundCloud track public
steps.what: Make the SoundCloud track public and turn on amplification.
steps.why: It reaches followers' feeds the same day as every other store, and amplification recommends it to about 100 listeners whose taste matches.
steps.how: If it isn't scheduled, switch the track to public. Then open the track page and turn on amplification.

steps.title: Post the release on every platform
steps.what: Post a release-day TikTok, Reel and Short using the official audio.
steps.why: YouTube says to always pick the official audio from the Shorts audio picker on release day, so views count toward the song.
steps.how: Pick the official sound in each app's audio picker rather than uploading the clip's own audio.

steps.title: Update your profile and share Promo Cards
steps.what: Point your Artist Pick and links at the live song, and share Spotify Promo Cards.
steps.why: Spotify's release guide lists these as release-day steps: they send visitors straight to the song.
steps.how: In Spotify for Artists, set the Artist Pick to the song. Make Promo Cards from the song page and share them in Stories.

steps.title: Send the track to a DJ promo pool
steps.what: Send the release to DJs through a promo pool.
steps.why: DJ support gets the track played out and shared in mixes. About $10 of the budget goes here.
steps.how: Upload the WAV to the pool with a short note about where the track works in a set.

steps.title: Release-day check-in
steps.what: Type in your follower counts on each platform.
steps.why: They are the baseline for working out how many followers this release gained.
steps.how: Open each app and note your follower count. Leave any you don't use blank.

steps.title: Keep posting after release
steps.what: Keep posting: daily for the first week, then about three a week until R+28.
steps.why: YouTube says it's "not just one and done": consistency is what keeps a sound moving. The exact cadence is a default, not a rule.
steps.how: Mix promo clips with reactions to comments and fan videos. Spread out the other visuals over the weeks.

steps.title: Repost and credit fan videos
steps.what: Find videos that use your sound and repost or reply to them.
steps.why: Thanking people who use the sound encourages more of them, and it gives you posts you didn't have to make.
steps.how: Open your sound's page on TikTok and Instagram, and repost or stitch the best ones with credit.

steps.title: R+7 check-in
steps.what: Type in the first week's numbers from Spotify, SoundCloud, TikTok and Instagram.
steps.why: Spotify frames day 7 as the first point to look at a release's stats. The app compares them with your past releases and suggests changes for the rest of the plan.
steps.how: Each field says where to find the number. Leave any field blank if you can't find it.

steps.title: Plan your next single
steps.what: If another track is ready, upload and pitch it now for a release at least four weeks out.
steps.why: The pitch slot frees up once this song is live, and a steady run of singles keeps followers' Release Radar fed without tiring curators.
steps.how: Start a new release in the app with a Friday at least four weeks away.

steps.title: Consider a Marquee campaign
steps.what: Run a Spotify Marquee campaign for the release, if you qualify and the numbers say it's worth it.
steps.why: Marquee shows the release to listeners in the Spotify app. It only runs within 21 days of release and needs 5,000 monthly listeners in the market and 1,000 streams in the last 28 days.
steps.how: In Spotify for Artists, open Campaigns and set up Marquee with part of the held-back budget.

steps.title: Last day for SoundCloud amplification
steps.what: Amplification must be turned on by today.
steps.why: SoundCloud only amplifies tracks made public within the last 14 days, on the Artist and Artist Pro plans.
steps.how: Open the track page on SoundCloud and check amplification is on. If not, turn it on now.

steps.title: Consider a Showcase campaign
steps.what: Run a Spotify Showcase campaign, if you qualify and something is working.
steps.why: Showcase promotes a release on Spotify's Home screen for 14 days. It needs 1,000 streams in the last 28 days.
steps.how: In Spotify for Artists, open Campaigns and set up Showcase with part of the held-back budget.

steps.title: R+28 check-in and retrospective
steps.what: Type in the 28-day numbers, including Spotify's release engagement, and read the retrospective.
steps.why: Release Radar exposure ends after four weeks, and Spotify shows release engagement at 28 days. The retrospective is what your next plan learns from.
steps.how: Each field says where to find the number. The app writes what worked, what didn't and 2 or 3 things to try next time.
